presets.name: Live lead vocal
presets.desc: Level-independent de-essing from 6 kHz, shelf cut up to 8 dB: holds when the singer backs off or a comp sits upstream

refs.why: FOH Brian Pomp puts a de-esser in the live lead vocal chain
refs.source: Vintage King, Brian Pomp FOH interview, 2017

presets.notes: The doc's live-lead row. Relative detection matters live: mic distance changes all night

presets.name: Bright high voice
presets.desc: Narrow bell at 7.5 kHz: a high, bright voice's sharp 's' notched out while the air above stays

presets.name: Low voice, lower sibilance
presets.desc: Detection from 4.5 kHz with a shelf: a deep voice's duller, lower 's' and 'sh' caught without lisping
presets.notes: Vocal focus's zero-crossing weight keeps bright vowels from triggering this lower band

presets.name: Heavy sibilance, wide band
presets.desc: 10:1 wide-band reduction up to 12 dB: a very sibilant singer or a bright condenser mic tamed hard
presets.notes: The doc's heavy row with Wide, which ducks the whole voice briefly: the cleanest-sounding way on a solo vocal

presets.name: Close-mic rap and speech
presets.desc: 5.5 kHz shelf, 8:1, fast 40 ms release: dense, close-mic'd rap or speech de-essed word by word
presets.notes: Fast delivery leaves no gap between esses: the short release keeps the next vowel from being dulled

presets.name: Transparent with lookahead
presets.desc: 5 ms lookahead catches the very start of each 's': fully transparent de-essing for playback or recording
presets.notes: Reports 5 ms of latency: not for a singer monitoring themselves in ears

presets.name: Overdrive fizz tamer
presets.desc: Allround high-frequency limiter, bell at 3.5 kHz: pick click and fizz of a driven guitar softened only when they spike
presets.notes: The doc's de-harsh row. After amp and cab: a static EQ cut would dull the palm mutes too

presets.name: Cymbal and hi-hat tamer
presets.desc: Allround shelf from 8 kHz: harsh crashes and hats on overheads or a drum bus pulled down only when they ring
presets.notes: Allround: no zero-crossing weight, cymbals are noise-like and must be treated as a whole
